data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'k-z-n', meaning 'to protect, defend, fortify'. In Islamic tradition, Kaza represents a strong and unwavering belief in Allah and one's faith. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kaza usually hope their child will grow to embody fortress, stronghold and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.name: كازا
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من كوز، بمعنى الخالق أو المقدر
in_arabic.long_meaning: كازا هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه الخالق أو المقدر، مشتق من فعل كوز الذي يعني الخلق أو التقدير. ورد في بعض المراجع اللغوية العربية أن الكوز هو اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى، و قد ذكر بعض العلماء أن هذا الاسم يوحي بالقدرة الإلهية على الخلق و التقدير.

in_urdu.name: کازا

Etymologically, it stems from the Arabic root 'k-w-z' which implies creation or predetermination. In Islamic tradition, the name Kaza holds spiritual significance as it reflects Allah's power and decree. Historically, names derived from divine attributes have been popular among Muslims for their sacred connotations. The name suggests qualities of omnipotence and sovereignty.
